changes: Create scalable floor tiles in Walls/Floor, with editable colors and embedded images that stretch to the tile bounds. Floors stay beneath every foreground object in editing, previews and exported maps.
Start new productions with empty scenes. Bundled demos, demo guide and demo reset controls are removed; saved and imported productions remain intact.

Import Production Desk shot-list CSVs with all supported source fields, including Script coverage. Reimport matching scene and shot numbers without duplicating them, retaining map objects, camera links, coverage checks and absent shots.
Preserve floor images through portable project save/import and native save/reopen, and keep floor controls usable in compact layouts.
Load The Last Light to explore eight screenplay scenes and sixteen linked shots shared with Production Desk.
Compare coastal road, station wagon and lighthouse layouts with camera setups, lighting and movement, plus the original screenplay in scene notes.
Import Production Desk shot-list CSV updates without duplicating scenes or shots, preserving map geometry, camera links and coverage checks.
Reopening the managed demo preserves edits. Reset affects only that demo and supports cancellation and Undo; imported copies and existing productions remain separate.

The fictional demo is included temporarily for beta testing and reference. Its entry point will be removed before production. Portable projects, touch placement and desktop update safeguards remain available.
Import shot list CSV now sits inside Shot List beside Export Shot List CSV. Both actions stay together as scenes change, with touch targets that fit narrow layouts.
Camera, light, person and sun Properties panels show less explanatory text while preserving every setting, default value, numerical readout and calculation.
Continue importing Production Desk shot lists and exporting CSVs with existing scene, camera-link and coverage information preserved.
The top-left Scenic brand now identifies the native device: iOS on iPhone, iPad on iPad, MacBook on Mac, and Desktop on Windows.
Platform labels remain correct when resizing or rotating, with the Scenic name visible in the compact phone header.
Existing productions, palette drag placement, portable .scenic exchange, and desktop updates remain available.
Drag cameras, talent, lights, room shapes and catalog items directly from the library or toolbar onto the scene map. Click or tap, then place, remains available.
On touch screens, hold briefly before dragging; swipe normally to scroll. Clear placement feedback follows the current pan, zoom and snapping, and cancelled drops add nothing.

On iPad, Scenes, Items and Properties have clear checked open states. Scenes sits beside Scene map and Shot list, and a saved Settings option keeps Scenes and Items on the left in landscape by default.
Load Demo opens The Last Cue as a separate offline fictional production with editable blocking, lighting, movement and four linked shots. Reopening the demo preserves your edits.
Keep item categories available while browsing and give iPhone catalog cards enough room for touch placement.
Continue editing and exchanging complete portable .scenic files across Mac, Windows, iPhone and iPad.
Save and share complete editable Scenic projects with all scenes, reference images, camera links, motion, shot lists and settings.
Import project files as separate editable productions, with safe duplicate naming and validation that preserves current work.
Exchange files with the iPhone and iPad apps; iPhone controls now adapt to compact screens.
Mac distributions are signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and include stapled tickets for Gatekeeper verification.
Import Production Desk shot-list CSVs, choose scenes, and create empty maps with all original shot and camera details.
Link cameras to imported shots and track coverage checks; reimport matching scene and shot numbers without duplicates while keeping camera setups, links, and checks.
Browse every scene in a production in a separate window with numbered, titled previews, and click a scene to switch to it.
Give the workspace more room by dragging the bottom of the top toolbar upward; Scenic remembers the height you choose.
Use a slimmer workspace header and a more compact left sidebar with a larger Scenic title, production credit, and Saved on your computer.
Match the blue Scenic logo and Mac Dock icon sizing to Production Desk.
Report bugs from Settings by email to alexanderhosier@squidproductions.org.
After an editor crash or unexpected shutdown, choose whether to send a crash report with a description of what happened.
Review or save crash logs before opening an email draft. Reopen the latest report from Settings; nothing is sent automatically.
See what is new before updating: Mac and Windows update prompts now include the release's changes.
Reopen What's New from Settings or the Scenic menu to review the installed version and recent changes offline.
Add room presets, edit individual walls, and group walls to move, resize, or rotate them together.
Box-select scene items to move, duplicate, or delete them together.
Turn talent with facing handles, aim cameras and lights directly, and preview camera coverage using lens and sensor dimensions.
Plan with improved real-world scale, editable talent footprints, and reference-image calibration.
Calculate sun direction offline using shoot location, date, time zone, and map north, or keep using manual Sun mode.
Gear is removed from the library and search; existing saved gear remains readable and editable.
